reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Using MGFA class as an outcome measure.
name: MGFA Clinical Classification of Myasthenia Gravis

version.label: MGFA clinical classification (Jaretzki et al. 2000)
version.detail: Classes I–V with subclasses a (limb/axial) and b (oropharyngeal/respiratory). Classes II–IV allow ocular weakness of any severity. The older Osserman classification is different.

purpose: Classifies the maximum severity and distribution of myasthenic weakness.

options.label: I: Ocular weakness only (may include eye closure); all other strength normal
IIa: Mild non-ocular weakness, predominantly limb and/or axial
IIb: Mild non-ocular weakness, predominantly oropharyngeal and/or respiratory
IIIa: Moderate non-ocular weakness, predominantly limb and/or axial
IIIb: Moderate non-ocular weakness, predominantly oropharyngeal and/or respiratory
IVa: Severe non-ocular weakness, predominantly limb and/or axial
IVb: Severe non-ocular weakness, predominantly oropharyngeal and/or respiratory (includes feeding tube without intubation)
V: Intubation, with or without mechanical ventilation (excluding routine postoperative care)

clinicalContext.text: Standard description of disease severity and pattern, used for trial entry and communication.

clinicalInsights.text: Bulbar or respiratory predominance: correlate with respiratory function and swallowing.

limitations.text: Designed to classify maximum severity; not a sensitive measure of change (use quantitative scales).

limitations: Mild, moderate and severe are not defined numerically.

confounders.effect: Classification at maximum severity versus current status differs.

guideSections.what: Five classes of myasthenic weakness, with a/b subclasses by distribution.
guideSections.howToPerform: Assess ocular, limb, axial, bulbar and respiratory weakness; choose the class.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Used with quantitative MG scores and respiratory monitoring.

sources.citation: Jaretzki A 3rd, Barohn RJ, Ernstoff RM, et al. Myasthenia gravis: recommendations for clinical research standards. Task Force of the Medical Scientific Advisory Board of the Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America. Neurology. 2000;55(1):16-23.
